speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Government will proactively engage displaced food and beverage operators to mitigate the ongoing shortage of canteen operators in schools; and (b) whether the Government will consider incentivising such pivots, providing these operators with stable, low-rental business environments while ensuring students have access to affordable quality meals.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry has considered paying individual hawkers to set up stalls in the school canteen to sell cooked food.

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan
text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to the Central Kitchen Meal Model where a single operator serves multiple schools (a) what risk assessment framework has the Ministry developed to address the concentration of food safety risk across multiple school populations; and (b) whether there is a cap on the number of schools a single central kitchen operator can supply to.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Minister can provide an update on the case where 147 North View Primary School pupils suffered suspected gastroenteritis symptoms; and (b) how the Ministry has been supporting affected students and their families.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: My response will also cover related oral and written questions filed for subsequent Sittings from Ms Lee Hui Ying, Ms Joan Pereira1, Ms Elysa Chen2 and Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: As parents and Members of this House, we all understand how important school meals are for our children's growth and well-being.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) is fully committed to ensuring that every student has access to affordable, nutritious and balanced meals.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: For decades, we have relied on individual stallholders running our canteen stalls – the familiar model many of us grew up with, where we fondly remember our favourite uncle or auntie serving our go-to dishes.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We always looked forward to recess and lunch.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: An increasing number of schools are struggling to fill their vacant canteen stalls, leaving students, especially those with dietary needs, very limited options.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: In some cases, these students may have to eat the same dish for weeks; and as parents, all of us would want our children to have a better experience.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Mr Louis Chua, Miss Rachel Ong, Ms Lee Hui Ying and Mr Foo Cexiang asked whether additional measures would be provided to sustain individual stallholders.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We also seek preferential electricity tariffs through demand aggregation and we pass these savings directly to stallholders.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We regularly review our food pricing guidelines to ensure that stallholder operations can remain viable while keeping the meals affordable for our students and their families.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: But the challenges go deeper than just costs.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: School canteens have a small customer base and limited business hours due to the school schedules.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Elderly stallholders may also start to have regular medical appointments and may not be able to operate their stalls daily.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: This is a complex issue with no easy solutions, but we will continue to explore new ways and different ways to support our stallholders.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about the number of schools that MOE expects to adopt the Central Kitchen Meal Model by 2030.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We did not start the Central Kitchen Meal Model so as to replace the traditional canteen model.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We wanted to explore alternative models to help our schools that were struggling to attract stallholders and had severe shortages of functioning stalls.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We want to avoid putting students in these schools at risk of not having good access to affordable, nutritious and balanced meals.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: So, we started with a pilot at Yusof Ishak Secondary School, which relocated from Bukit Batok to Punggol and did not have existing stallholders at the Punggol site.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: After seeing positive results, we decided to try out a range of Central Kitchen Meal Models in 13 additional schools that faced challenges in securing sufficient stallholders.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: This allowed students in these schools to continue to have access to healthy and affordable food options.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Elysa Chen asked about our openness to other models.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We are indeed taking an open and flexible approach, and hence, we are trying out a range of possible models.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Some schools are using hybrid models, where operators both deliver pre-ordered meals as well as prepare fresh food onsite.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: In several schools, students can still choose and watch their meals being prepared at live cooking stations, alongside having the pre-ordered options.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We will continue to look at different options that best serve our students’ needs and refine the model based on feedback.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We do see some positive outcomes in our schools.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Students spend less time queuing for food during recess and have more time for play and interaction with one another.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Parents have also shared that they now know what their children eat in school and can better support their children in achieving a balanced diet.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Our teachers also now have access to a wider range of meal options in school.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We appreciate the concern that many Members have shown towards the stallholders affected by the transition in schools that are trying out the new models.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I want to assure Members that our schools have been actively supporting the stallholders throughout this process.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Several of them have joined our three operators and now enjoy more stable income.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Others have found placements at different schools, pursued new opportunities, or chosen to retire.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: MOE continues to welcome applications from anyone interested in operating school canteen stalls, including private entities for schools with persistent vacancies.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: All available opportunities are listed on our website.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Several Members asked about food safety measures and the applicable good hygiene standard.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Food prepared by central kitchens is not inherently unsafe or less safe.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Central kitchens are licensed by the Singapore Food Agency (SFA).

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: They are subjected to more frequent inspections, as explained by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Goh Hanyan, as they have a larger scale of food processing or preparation.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: In addition, central kitchens are graded under the Safety Assurance for Food Establishment framework.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: In the event of a major food lapse, they will be downgraded and inspected even more frequently.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: MOE will continue to work with SFA, the Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA) and the operators to strengthen food safety management systems.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: This covers everything from preparation at the central kitchens to transportation, storage and eventually, when the food is served to the students.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying asked for data on gastroenteritis cases from January 2022 to December 2025.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Many Members also asked about the recent suspected gastroenteritis incidents in River Valley Primary School and North View Primary School.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: SFA, CDA and MOE are still investigating the causes for both incidents.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: River Valley Primary School currently uses one of our Central Kitchen Meal Model operators, while North View Primary School has traditional stallholders.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Both schools immediately stepped up the cleaning and sanitisation of their canteens and premises.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Students were also reminded about good personal hygiene and to rest at home if they are unwell.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Throughout both incidents, the schools maintained close, regular communication with parents and caregivers and continue to work vigilantly with SFA and CDA to monitor any developments.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: At both schools, all affected students have returned to school.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: While the investigations continue, we have reinforced with the Central Kitchen Meal Model operator at River Valley Primary School and also with the stallholders at North View Primary School the critical importance of maintaining the highest food safety standards and full compliance with SFA requirements.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: This includes kitchen cleanliness and safe food handling practices.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Ms Eileen Chong and Mr Fadli Fawzi asked about our protocols for suspension, termination and contingency measures.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Operations may be suspended or terminated for severe food safety breaches or ongoing disease transmission, with other punitive actions considered based on the findings.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: For schools using our Central Kitchen Meal Model operators, MOE has established contingency protocols to ensure that students will continue to have access to school meals.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: This helps to contain the impact of any operational issues and also allows us to observe different operators' performance and have back-up options ready if needed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State, if I could just interrupt you for a moment.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I believe Leader wishes to move a Motion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: SUSPENSION OF STANDING ORDERS (Extension of Question Time)

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: ENHANCING FOOD SAFETY MEASURES FOLLOWING RECENT GASTROENTERITIS CASES AT PRIMARY SCHOOLS AND INCENTIVES FOR OPERATORS OF SCHOOL CANTEENS (Resumption for Question Nos 14 to 20)

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: While the Central Kitchen Meal Model operators have had some initial pre-ordering problems in the first few weeks, the situation has stabilised.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We will continue to monitor the performance of the operators closely and also actively take in feedback from students, parents and teachers.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I want to end by thanking Members for the concern for our students and for the stallholders, and for the many good suggestions that had come in.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We are committed to providing every student access to affordable and healthy meal options in our schools.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We will continue to listen, to learn and to adapt to serve and support our children better.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Speaker, it is rather unfortunate that we have experienced two incidents at the very early stage of the school reopening, where many of our little ones, especially the Primary 1 students have just entered schools, and the incidents happened in primary schools in this instance.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I believe this has invariably caused some anxiety for parents, especially for those whose children have just entered primary schools for the very first time.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, can I ask the Ministry, how has MOE worked with the schools to communicate updates to the parents and what has been the feedback received thus far in relation to the handling of these issues on the ground in the schools?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second supplementary question is whether, following from these incidents, we are ramping up our efforts in raising more awareness and encouraging our students to practise good personal hygiene?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: First, when suspected incidents do happen, the schools monitor the well-being of the students very closely through daily checks on attendance or when students exhibit or report symptoms.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: They then check with students who are absent from class to make sure that the students are okay, or to check in if there is a pattern of the cases emerging.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Both cases are still under investigation, so we are not able to say for certainty if the incidents resulted from the operators' management of the food or from the stallholders' management of the food.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: But indeed, in both cases, the schools have reminded the students about good personal hygiene and have communicated throughout the incidents with parents to assure them that sanitation and cleaning has been done throughout the school premises.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We definitely hope to do more education about food safety, but also about the Central Kitchen Meal Model in general to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: Again, because this is really to ensure that all students have access to good and affordable options.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are still many Members who wish to ask questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: While we have extended Question Time, my request is to Members as well as Minister of State Lau to keep the questions and the answers succinct.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But my supplementary question has to do with the quality of meals, specifically along the dimension of variety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As a parent of a very picky six-year-old eater, I am sympathetic to arguments that that the kind of food that the central kitchen may serve up on any given day may simply be forgone by such students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Setting aside how we really need to expand our daughter's palate, is the Ministry concerned that the central kitchen model may inadvertently give rise to nutritional deficiencies among a certain segment of this student population?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: In fact, many parents of students who are in the schools with Central Kitchen Meal Models now do say that now they know what their kids are eating in school and they are able to view the meal options as well as the nutritional value of the meals through the apps where they do the pre-ordering.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister of State for her really empathetic response and I, in particular, appreciate the support that MOE has given our individual stallholders.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My supplementary question is really my main question, which is, has MOE considered paying individual hawkers to set up stalls in the canteen?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And I ask that for the same reason that Minister of State raised in the speech, because if our objective is affordable, nutritious and balanced meals, I can understand that where you do not have individual food stallers who want to do so, you turn to the central kitchen model.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But if our objective on top of that is the positive school experience where the canteen and school is a microcosm society of the hawker centres in the public spaces, then where there is a dearth of individual stallholders, would it not be then time for the Government to consider paying people to provide this experience for our students?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: But we are not closed to the idea of any model at all out there that could give our students access to good, affordable and healthy food.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Second, the Minister of State mentioned that challenges for traditional kitchens go beyond cost.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: How will the Government make the traditional canteen model more attractive for vendors?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: But indeed, if the results do show that, I think we would definitely have to take a look to ensure that central kitchen models do not undermine the safety of the food that we give to our students.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: I mentioned in my reply earlier that we will look at all types of ways to support our stallholders better.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: As Mr Foo Cexiang had asked, we are open to all possible models, including paying the stallholders, if need be, to and again, ensure that our students have good access to healthy and affordable food.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Will the Government consider making similar nutrition and safety roles accredited professionals?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The second supplementary question: I quote The Straits Times on their reporting of the River Valley Primary school case, "Some parents told ST that their children had noticed the chicken on the pizza tasting a bit strange.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: A few parents said their children were fine after consuming the pizza as they had picked the chicken off.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: A pupil told his mother that the chicken did not smell good but he ate it anyway and had diarrhoea the next day." So, can I just ask what is the status of the investigation into the chicken?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: If it was the chicken, how did it make it past the food hygiene officer?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: On dietary teachers, I think that was the term the Member used, and food safety officers, in Singapore, we do work closely with the Health Promotion Board to ensure that the food that we provide to all our students from preschool to primary school to secondary schools have good nutritional value and meet the needs of our students.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We also have food hygiene officers in our schools with the Central Kitchen Meal Models, and they do make checks on the way that the food is handled to make sure that the food is safe.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State Janil, did you want to make a clarification?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
